AndAlso/OrElse do propagate nulls normally too, no? Like if you do c.a AND c.b, the expression returns NULL if one of the operands is null?
Are there other unary operators that propagate? Maybe better to exclude those that you don't want, rather than specifying those that you do?

Interestingly, if the node isn't nullable, then the checks can also be elided - though that elision sould take place elsewhere. This makes me think that we can introduce some basic simplifications in SqlExpressionFactory.IsNull/IsNotNull, recognizing the basic non-nullable node types...

DetectNullPropagatingNodes currently treats all binary operators except AndAlso/OrElse as null-propagating. This includes ExpressionType.Coalesce, which is not null-propagating (e.g., COALESCE(a, '') can be non-null even when a is null). That can cause DropNotNullChecks to incorrectly remove a IS NOT NULL predicates and change query semantics. Handle ExpressionType.Coalesce explicitly (do not treat its left operand as null-propagating), and consider auditing any other non-null-propagating binary operators represented as SqlBinaryExpression.
